claims.claim: For a fixed finite local endotactic reaction family in fixed species dimension d, the supplied deterministic affine-barrier corollary yields a compact positive invariant range K for any number of compartments when each edge uses the same scalar transport coefficient for every species. K is independent of graph size, topology, and the magnitude of locally bounded edge coefficients, including coefficients proportional to h^-2.

interface.initial_data: Each cell concentration belongs to one fixed compact Q0 subset of the positive orthant.
interface.reaction: A fixed finite local reaction family, with bounded supplied rates; the source's common-species transport corollary permits local measurable mixtures.
interface.transport: Nonnegative locally bounded scalar edge coefficients, identical across species on each edge.

claims.proof: The local affine minimum F_s uses fixed slopes r_lambda in R^d. For G=min_(v,lambda) L_(lambda,s)(x_v), an active label at v satisfies L_(lambda,s)(x_w)>=G=L_(lambda,s)(x_v) for every w. Hence r_lambda dot sum_w m_vw(x_w-x_v)=sum_w m_vw(L_(lambda,s)(x_w)-L_(lambda,s)(x_v))>=0. The reaction derivative at an active label is nonnegative; the source's compact plateau is therefore invariant. The sign proof is independent of N_h and m_vw.
claims.consequence: A mesh family with concentrations initially in Q0 has an h-independent all-time L-infinity bound and positive coordinate lower bound.
limitations: This is invariant-range confinement from bounded positive initial profiles, not an all-data classwise absorber or a uniform entry time for arbitrary spatially unbounded initial data.
PDE convergence still needs a specified consistent mesh, discrete coercivity/compactness, and convergence of h-dependent reaction controls.
claims.source: Local 7 October reconstruction, d-326696af15b5e02b.html, sections 'Switching, convex mixtures, and invariant transport' and 'Common-species transport on arbitrary finite topologies', especially lines 739-924.

claims.claim: Under shape-regular quasi-uniform finite-volume assumptions on a fixed bounded domain, the common-scalar invariant range gives a subsequential reaction-diffusion PDE limit that remains in the same compact positive convex K. The same conclusion holds for diagonal species diffusion when every facet normal of K is a common nonnegative left eigenvector of every edge diffusion matrix and the diffusivities are uniformly elliptic.

uniformity_criterion.transport_normal_test: For each facet normal a_i and edge matrix A^h_vw, require (a_i)^T A^h_vw=mu^h_i,vw (a_i)^T with mu^h_i,vw>=0.
uniformity_criterion.reaction_test: At each site, the local reaction field points into K on each active facet; uniform boundedness on K is required for compactness.
uniformity_criterion.mesh_test: Symmetric conservative consistent graph Laplacian; discrete H1 energy equivalent to the piecewise-constant gradient; diffusivities bounded below; initial interpolants converge in L2.
uniformity_criterion.controls_test: For the finite reaction list, coefficient fields are fixed or have a weak-* convergent subsequence.

claims.proof: The eigenvector condition turns edge transport on facet i into sum_w mu_i,vw [g_i(x_w)-g_i(x_v)]>=0 whenever x_v is on that facet and all x_w are in K, so Q^N is invariant. Uniform boundedness of reactions on K and the symmetric diffusion identity yield a uniform L-infinity_t L2_x bound and an integrated discrete H1 bound. The equation bounds time derivatives in discrete H^-1. Standard discrete Rellich/Aubin-Lions compactness gives a strongly L2-convergent subsequence; closed convexity of K gives u(t,x) in K almost everywhere. Strong concentration convergence and weak-* rate convergence pass the bounded polynomial reactions to the weak PDE.
claims.limitation: This is a conditional compactness and limit statement, not supplied as a theorem by the reaction-network source.

claims.claim: For the stochastic graph exit estimate with a transported facet, D_h=kappa h^-2 and bounded degree give eta_i(h)=Theta(h^2), Q_i(h)=Theta(h^-2), theta_i(h)=Theta(h^2), rho_i(h)=Theta(h^4), and B_i(h)=O(1). The displayed estimate is useful uniformly over N_h~h^-p sites and time T only if V_h h^4 dominates log N_h+log(V_h T), in addition to the source's fixed local V_h>=V0 requirement.
claims.exact_bound: P(tau_Q<=T)<=N_h sum_i exp(-V_h theta_i(h) zeta_i)+V_h T N_h sum_i B_i(h) exp(-V_h rho_i(h)).
claims.physical_scaling: If local volume V_h=Omega_h h^p, then the load-bearing exponent is Omega_h h^(p+4). Fixed Omega_h=Omega violates V_h>=V0 as h->0 and sends the formal exponent to zero. A polynomial high-density scaling sufficient for this certificate is Omega_h h^(p+4)/log(1/h)->infinity for fixed T.
claims.reaction_rescaling: A reaction changes concentration by nu/V_h and fires at intensity V_h k phi^V_y(X), so the drift is k phi^V_y(X)nu -> k X^y nu. The finite-volume factorial correction is at most D_i/V_h with D_i=K sum_r |a_i dot nu_r| E_(y_r)(U); V_h>=V0=max(1,max_i ceil(2D_i/gamma_i)) preserves half the supplied margin. This local threshold is independent of N_h but fails under fixed-density voxel scaling V_h=Omega h^p.

claims.claim: The local strict-inward reaction polytope Q={1<=x<=3, 1<=y<=3, x+y>=3} is not automatically invariant under species-dependent transport, even with linear reactions 0<->A and 0<->B having drift (2-x,2-y). On two sites, A hopping at alpha/h^2 and B at beta/h^2 with beta>alpha gives both sites initial lower-sum-facet gap epsilon; the first-site facet gap becomes negative by time c h^2 for the explicit h-range below.
claims.active_facet: The first site exits through the lower sum facet x_(1,A)+x_(1,B)-3=0. Both initial site gaps are exactly epsilon>0.
claims.parameters: alpha=1, beta=3, c=log(3)/4, epsilon=1/1000 give g_h(c h^2)=1-(1-epsilon)e^(-c h^2)(1+1/(3 sqrt(3)))<0 whenever h^2<(4/log(3))*log[(999/1000)(1+1/(3 sqrt(3)))], a positive threshold about 0.63720237. Since g_h(0)=epsilon>0, the exact certified upper bound on the first exit time is tau_h<=c h^2; the first zero need not equal c h^2. The limit is epsilon-(1-epsilon)/(3 sqrt(3))<0.
claims.independent_exact_check: At h=1 and t=log(100/99), the gap is -1621541844091699/200000000000000000. This rational value was recomputed exactly with fractions.
claims.continuum_falsifier: For D_A=3,D_B=1 and initial profiles x=3/2-(1/10)(1-cos(4z)), y=3/2+(1/5)(1-cos(4z)), the smooth positive data lie in Q and touch the sum facet at z=0. There the PDE gap derivative is 1+3(-16/10)+16/5=-3/5, so the solution immediately leaves Q.
claims.scope_limit: This falsifies transfer of this product-polytope/affine certificate. It does not show absence of another absorber or failure of permanence for the stable linear example.

claims.claim: The affine family uses a finite slope set fixed before its auxiliary scale and lies in local dimension d. Its strict drift in the scale box is delta_s=kappa H s^M after K L s^H<=kappa H, and the plateau lies within [sqrt(s),s^-1/2]^d. For a fixed local network these constants do not depend on mesh size when reused sitewise; the source supplies no useful uniform lower bounds on H or s_P, or upper bounds on W_s, across varying network families or if the whole dN graph is treated as one growing-dimensional network.
claims.consequence: The sitewise common-scalar transport corollary is the valid route to h-uniform confinement; silently applying the single-network absorber theorem in dimension dN does not establish uniform constants.

claims.claim: There are smooth positive initial data on T^3 with unit local mass, zero local momentum, and local energy 3, such that epsilon^-2 H(f_epsilon^in|M)->0 but the order-three energy flux of g_epsilon^in diverges in distributions in x.
claims.quantifiers: For all sufficiently small epsilon>0, use a(x)=1+0.5 sin(2*pi*x_1), R=epsilon^-4, delta=epsilon^12 a(x), U=-delta R e_1/(1-delta), T=1-delta R^2/[3(1-delta)^2], and f=(1-delta)N(U,T I)+delta N(R e_1,I). Then epsilon^-2 H=O(epsilon^2), while pairing int (|v|^2/2)v M g_epsilon^in dv against grad cos(2*pi*x_1) equals -pi/(4 epsilon)+O(epsilon^11).
claims.dependency: Gaussian mass/momentum/energy identities; convexity of relative entropy; Gaussian KL and third-moment formulas.

claims.scope: Falsifies entropy-only control of this flux passage. It does not prove that the hydrodynamic limit fails.

claims.claim: The same initial family converges entropically at order epsilon to g^in=0 in the local weak topology used by the cited theorem.
claims.quantifiers: Uniformly in x, ||f_epsilon^in(x,.)-M||_L1(dv)=O(epsilon^4); on every compact velocity set, g_epsilon^in->0 strongly in L1(dx dv); epsilon^-2 H(f_epsilon^in|M)->0=(1/2)int M|0|^2.
claims.dependency: Total-variation continuity of Gaussian densities for T near 1 and U near 0; tail mixture mass delta=O(epsilon^12).
claims.falsifier: Failure of local L1 convergence or of the stated entropy scaling for the given formula.
claims.scope: Initial-data entropic convergence only; no solution-level compactness is asserted.

claims.claim: The initial entropy convergence assumptions do not imply the initial-time analogue of the cited general-data Euler theorem's pointwise L2(M^-1) tail bound.
claims.quantifiers: For the data in C1 and every x, int M((f_epsilon^in-M)/M)^2 dv >= delta(x)^2 exp(R^2)-1 >= (epsilon^24/4)exp(epsilon^-8)-1 -> infinity.
claims.dependency: Gaussian chi-square identity for N(R e_1,I) relative to N(0,I), and f_epsilon^in>=delta N(R e_1,I).
claims.falsifier: A correction to the Gaussian likelihood-ratio integral or mixture lower bound.
claims.scope: Theorem 2.1 imposes its bound on the solution for almost every positive time. The t=0 calculation alone does not show that the actual solution violates that a.e.-in-time assumption; positive-time regularization is not analyzed here.

claims.claim: Saint-Raymond's 2009 Theorem 2.1 is a primary-source incompressible Euler limit for general entropically convergent initial fluctuations, with an additional uniform large-velocity bound on the solution family.
claims.quantifiers: For smooth bounded Omega or T^3 and a measurable a.e.-positive Grad-cutoff kernel 0<b(z,omega)<=Cb(1+|z|)^beta with int_S2 b(z,omega)domega>=Cb^-1|z|/(1+|z|), beta in [0,1], let q>1. Assume epsilon^-2 H(f_epsilon^in|M)<=C, g_epsilon^in weakly convergent locally and epsilon^-2 H->(1/2)int M|g^in|^2, plus int M((f_epsilon-M)/M)^2 dv<=C for a.e. (t,x). Then fluctuations are relatively weakly compact; each limit is an infinitesimal Maxwellian whose fields solve incompressible Euler and a transported thermal scalar, with a fast acoustic corrector and strong corrected L1_loc convergence, up to the target solution lifespan. The field data are rho^in=int M g^in, u^in=int v M g^in, theta^in=(1/3)int(|v|^2-3)M g^in; u(0)=P u^in and theta(0)=(3theta^in-2rho^in)/5.
claims.dependency: Saint-Raymond 2009, Theorem 2.1 and proof equations (3.29)-(3.35); collision entropy inequality; modulated entropy; tail/dissipation estimates; Lipschitz target flow.
claims.falsifier: A contrary theorem statement in the cited primary paper or a mismatch between its assumptions and this transcription.
claims.scope: Imported theorem statement; not independently re-proved. We instantiate q=2 and the hard-sphere kernel.

claims.claim: The high-velocity condition in the general-data theorem is used to close an energy-flux estimate that relative entropy alone cannot close.
claims.quantifiers: Saint-Raymond states that g_epsilon |v|^3 is not controlled by relative entropy and uses a Chapman-Enskog decomposition plus tail and entropy-dissipation control; for q>1 the proof gains epsilon^((q-1)/2), equal to epsilon^1/2 at q=2.
claims.dependency: Saint-Raymond 2009, discussion preceding Theorem 2.1 and proof equations (3.32)-(3.34); C1-C3 show entropy convergence does not itself control the flux.
claims.falsifier: A proof of the same distributional energy-flux bound from assumptions (a)-(b) alone, covering the explicit family in C1.
claims.scope: Indispensability is established for this flux-closure inference, not for the truth of Euler convergence under weaker hypotheses.

claims.claim: The 2003 well-prepared incompressible Euler theorem is consistent with the counterexample and does not identify the high-order flux at t=0.
claims.quantifiers: For smooth divergence-free u^in and epsilon^-2 H(f_epsilon^in|M_{1,epsilon u^in,1})->0, renormalized solutions with q>1 have fluctuation limits u dot v on the lifespan of the Lipschitz Euler solution. The constructed data meet this initial entropy condition for u^in=0.

scope.model: One-dimensional Vlasov equation with K(r)=r^2/2, force K'(x-y)=x-y, and its N-particle empirical system.

claims.statement: For fixed T<infinity, the tagged position marginal rho^N_{1,t} is O_T(N^-1) close in W1 to the Vlasov position marginal rho_t, uniformly for 0<=t<=T.
claims.evidence: q(t)=cosh(2t), q_N(t)=(1-1/N)cosh(2t)+(1+t^2)/N; W1=sqrt(2/pi)(sqrt(q)-sqrt(q_N)) and is bounded by sqrt(2/pi)cosh(2T)/N.

claims.statement: At t_N=log(N)+c, for each fixed real c, W1(rho^N_{1,t_N},rho_{t_N}) tends to exp(c)/(2sqrt(pi)); hence uniform-in-time tagged chaos in W1 fails.
claims.evidence: At t_N, q/N^2->exp(2c)/2 and (q-q_N)/N->exp(2c)/2; rationalizing square roots yields the limit.

claims.statement: For each finite N the tagged position W1 error diverges as t->infinity, asymptotic to exp(t)/sqrt(pi)*(1-sqrt(1-1/N)).
claims.evidence: q(t)~exp(2t)/2 and q_N(t)/q(t)->1-1/N.

claims.statement: The Vlasov solution map has no time-independent W1 Lipschitz stability constant on centered Gaussian initial laws near Normal(0,I_2).
claims.evidence: Scale data by a; position W1 at time t is sqrt(2/pi)|a-1|sqrt(cosh(2t)), while initial phase W1<=2sqrt(2/pi)|a-1|. The ratio is >=0.5sqrt(cosh(2t))~exp(t)/(2sqrt(2)).

detailed_claim_record.claim: For the specified one-dimensional harmonic mean-field Langevin particle system with iid initial vectors of finite covariance, the empirical mean fluctuation has exact N^(1/2) scaling and covariance governed by the 2x2 Lyapunov equation C'=AC+CA^T+sigma^2 e2 e2^T.
detailed_claim_record.full_quantifiers: For every N>=1, gamma>0, omega>0, sigma>0, kappa in R, and iid Z_0^i in R^2 with mean m_0 and covariance Sigma_0, define A=[[0,1],[-(omega^2-kappa),-gamma]]. Then G_N=sqrt(N)(M_N-m) solves dG_N=AG_N dt+sigma e_2 dW_N exactly, and Cov(G_N(t))=C(t) for all t>=0, where C(0)=Sigma_0 and C'=AC+CA^T+sigma^2 e_2e_2^T. For finite fourth initial moment, the associated finite-test empirical fluctuation field converges in C([0,T]) for every fixed T<infinity and finite family of compactly supported smooth tests to the Gaussian weak SPDE specified in RESULT.txt.
detailed_claim_record.supplied_inputs: N, gamma, omega, kappa, sigma, iid initial law; independent Brownian motions.
detailed_claim_record.proof: Summing the particle equations gives the exact mean SDE. The standard iid vector CLT gives the initial Gaussian fluctuation; the normalized sum of Brownian motions is standard Brownian. Matrix Itô gives the covariance ODE. For the finite-test field, synchronously couple particles to iid nonlinear copies, represent the interaction as a common linear shift, apply the iid functional CLT to finitely many test processes, and Taylor-expand smooth tests. The empirical weak equation has a quadratic remainder of order N^(-1/2) times a tight product on each fixed horizon.
detailed_claim_record.costs: 2x2 matrix exponential/Lyapunov calculation; one global mean and O(N) local drift arithmetic per numerical time step. Exact-real analysis only; no parameter acquisition or discretization error is claimed.
detailed_claim_record.matched_baseline: The iid nonlinear copies driven by the same initial samples and Brownian motions and the supplied deterministic mean path.
detailed_claim_record.falsifier: An exact solution contradicting the summed mean SDE, covariance integral, or weak test covariance equation under the stated model and moments.

detailed_claim_record.claim: If both the centered kinetic matrix A_0 and mean matrix A are Hurwitz, the expected error for each fixed 1-Lipschitz observable is O(N^(-1/2)) uniformly over all t>=0, with an explicit constant.
detailed_claim_record.full_quantifiers: For every fixed gamma>0, omega>0, sigma>0, kappa<omega^2, iid initial Z_0 with finite covariance Sigma_0, every N>=1, every deterministic f:R^2->R with Lip(f)<=1, and every t>=0, choose M_0,M_A>=1 and rho_0,rho_A>0 such that ||e^(A_0t)||<=M_0e^(-rho_0t) and ||e^(At)||<=M_Ae^(-rho_At). Set K=M_0^2(tr(Sigma_0)+sigma^2/(2rho_0)). Then E|mu_t^N(f)-mu_t(f)| <= sqrt(K)(1+|kappa|M_A/rho_A)/sqrt(N). The same constant bounds sup_{t>=0}sup_{Lip(f)<=1} E|mu_t^N(f)-mu_t(f)|; it is not a bound on E[W_1].
detailed_claim_record.supplied_inputs: Stable model parameters and iid initial law with finite covariance.
detailed_claim_record.proof: The centered nonlinear copies have uniformly bounded second moment K. Their sample mean deviation Y_N has L2 norm at most sqrt(K/N). The common particle-to-copy shift solves Delta'=A Delta+kappa e2 Y_N^x. Semigroup decay and Minkowski yield ||Delta||_L2<=|kappa|M_A sqrt(K)/(rho_A sqrt(N)). The iid empirical sampling term for each 1-Lipschitz f has expected absolute value at most sqrt(K/N).
detailed_claim_record.costs: The displayed constant depends on semigroup decay and nonnormal conditioning. It becomes large near a zero eigenvalue. No entropy, log-Sobolev, or oracle cost is charged.
detailed_claim_record.matched_baseline: Iid nonlinear copies with the same information and noise; their sampling contribution is explicitly separated from the common interaction shift.
detailed_claim_record.falsifier: For a stable parameter choice, an exact evaluation of the left side exceeding the stated right side refutes the bound.

scope: kinetic linear response and closing spectral gap
claim: The exact OU response obeys fluctuation-dissipation while its zero-frequency susceptibility diverges as the damping gap closes.

detailed_claim_record.statement: For every m>0, T_b>0, gamma>0 and spatially homogeneous velocity Kramers-Fokker-Planck equation with force F(t), initialized at its Maxwellian equilibrium and differentiated at F=0, the current response kernel is chi_gamma(t)=1_{t>=0} exp(-gamma t)/m. Its causal resolvent is chi_tilde_gamma(z)=1/[m(z+gamma)] for Re(z)>0. The equilibrium velocity covariance is C_gamma(t)=(k_B T_b/m)exp(-gamma t) for t>=0, so chi_gamma(t)=beta C_gamma(t) exactly.
assumptions_and_quantifiers: m,T_b,gamma are fixed positive real numbers for each member of the family.
beta=(k_B T_b)^(-1), sigma^2=(beta m)^(-1), M is the centered Gaussian with variance sigma^2.
f is normalized; integrations by parts have vanishing velocity-boundary terms.
The observable is mean velocity and the input is force, with force entering the acceleration as F/m.
The response means the derivative at zero applied force, at fixed gamma; position and nonuniform spatial modes are outside the stated model.
detailed_claim_record.proof_pointer: RESULT.txt, sections 'Linear response and resolvent' and 'Fluctuation–dissipation identity and proof'. The first Hermite mode vM is invariant, L(vM)=-gamma vM; the OU SDE gives the covariance directly.

supplied_vs_acquired.note: This is an analytic model calculation, not an empirically fitted response.

costs.analytic_arithmetic: O(1) scalar operations after the parameters are supplied
costs.precision: For chi(0)=1/(m gamma), relative parameter errors propagate at first order as |Delta chi|/|chi| <= |Delta m|/m + |Delta gamma|/gamma. An absolute gamma error |Delta gamma| <= epsilon*m*gamma^2 suffices locally for absolute response error epsilon.
costs.trajectory_acquisition_if_empirical: A time horizon gamma^(-1) log(1/epsilon) is needed to observe decay to relative level epsilon; sample-count cost is not derived.

equal_input_baseline.direct_kinetic_method: Solve the linearized PDE; chi(t)=exp(-gamma t)/m and step response at T is (1-exp(-gamma T))/(m gamma).
equal_input_baseline.equilibrium_fluctuation_method: Compute C(t)=(k_B T_b/m)exp(-gamma t); beta*C(t) and beta*integral_0^T C(s) ds reproduce the same impulse and step responses.
equal_input_baseline.outcome: Exact algebraic agreement for every admitted parameter and finite horizon; this is an internal matched calculation, not external validation.

detailed_claim_record.falsifier: For any m,T_b,gamma>0, a disagreement between the direct first-order PDE solution and beta times the equilibrium velocity covariance under the same conventions falsifies the identity.

detailed_claim_record.statement: At fixed m>0 and T_b>0, the homogeneous OU kinetic family has exact mean-zero spectral gap gamma and static current susceptibility chi_tilde_gamma(0)=1/(m gamma). Hence the zero-frequency response is not uniformly bounded over gamma>0 as the gap closes, although for each fixed gamma>0 the response kernel decays exponentially and every fixed-time step response is finite. This one-mode example is sharp because source and observable both occupy the slow first Hermite mode.
assumptions_and_quantifiers: Fix m,T_b>0 and let gamma range over all positive values.
Static susceptibility is the derivative of stationary mean velocity with respect to constant force, equivalently the zero-frequency causal response integral.
Finite-time response is evaluated at a fixed horizon independent of gamma. No uniform-in-gamma exponential-decay claim is made.
detailed_claim_record.proof_pointer: RESULT.txt, sections 'Linear response and resolvent' and 'Gap-closing conclusion and sharpness'. For fixed T_f, |delta j(T_f)| <= |F_0|T_f/m, while chi_tilde_gamma(0)=1/(m gamma) diverges.

costs.model_size: One exact invariant Hermite mode; O(1) analytic expression.
costs.finite_time_acquisition: For empirical resolution of an epsilon-relative decay, the observation horizon scales at least gamma^(-1)log(1/epsilon).
costs.precision: Absolute precision for the parameter gamma must scale as epsilon*m*gamma^2 to guarantee absolute error epsilon in 1/(m gamma), locally.

detailed_claim_record.equal_input_baseline: Direct current response and the equilibrium Green-Kubo/FDT integral use identical m,T_b,gamma and give exactly 1/(m gamma). At m=k_B T_b=F_0=T_f=1, gamma=1,0.1,0.01 give finite-horizon step responses approximately 0.6321206,0.9516258,0.9950166 and static values 1,10,100.
detailed_claim_record.falsifier: The explicit resolvent formula would have to fail for some gamma>0, or a claimed gamma-uniform finite bound would have to coexist with 1/(m gamma) for arbitrarily small positive gamma.
detailed_claim_record.scientific_boundary: This refutes a general inference from pointwise relaxation/finite-time boundedness to uniform dc control. It does not imply divergence for every gap-closing kinetic model; vanishing slow-mode overlap can change the outcome.
unresolved: Whether a specific non-OU kinetic model has nonvanishing overlap with its slow modes requires separate analysis.
No novelty or priority claim.

detailed_claim_record.statement: For a reversible equilibrium generator L with discrete mean-zero spectral expansion L psi_k=-lambda_k psi_k, lambda_k>0, and a matched force-response source/observable A for which the FDT pairing holds and the inverse-generator quadratic form is finite, the zero-frequency response is beta*sum_k |<A,psi_k>|^2/lambda_k. A positive gap lower bound gives a norm-over-gap bound; closing gaps alone give no uniform bound unless the overlap weights on slow modes also suppress the inverse rates.
assumptions_and_quantifiers: L is self-adjoint and nonpositive on the mean-zero equilibrium Hilbert space.
The perturbation is conjugate to A so the response kernel is beta*<A,exp(tL)A>.
The spectral sum is interpreted by the spectral theorem and is finite for each model under consideration.
detailed_claim_record.proof_pointer: Expand A in the orthonormal eigenbasis and integrate beta*sum_k |<A,psi_k>|^2 exp(-lambda_k t) termwise when the nonnegative integral is finite; monotone convergence gives the stated sum.

costs.information: Requires the equilibrium generator, observable/source overlap, and spectral measure; these are supplied in the conditional statement.
costs.precision: A finite truncation needs control of the omitted low-rate spectral mass; no uniform truncation algorithm or cost is claimed.

limits: Continuous spectral measures require the corresponding integral formulation.
Non-reversible systems may have non-normal resolvent growth not captured by eigenvalues alone.

scope: Curie–Weiss critical fluctuations and thermodynamic limit
claim: Curie–Weiss critical fluctuations are quartic with Var(M)~1.1708286566 N^(3/2); coexistence is two-phase with susceptibility of order N.

detailed_claim_record.claim: For every N, beta>=0, and h in R, the Curie-Weiss Ising Gibbs law on sigma in {-1,+1}^N has magnetization mass proportional to binom(N,(N+M)/2) exp(beta M^2/(2N)+hM), and its thermodynamic pressure is the supremum in RESULT.txt equation (2).
detailed_claim_record.quantifiers: All positive integers N, all beta>=0, all h real; M ranges over {-N,-N+2,...,N}. For fixed beta,h, N^-1 log Z converges to sup_{|m|<=1}{log2-I(m)+beta*m^2/2+h*m}.
detailed_claim_record.constants_costs: Exact finite law has N+1 terms. Recurrence computes weights in O(N) arithmetic operations and O(N) memory; no observations or oracle are required. This excludes physical Gibbs preparation and finite-bit costs.
detailed_claim_record.evidence: Direct magnetization multiplicity count; standard thermodynamic variational limit. See RESULT.txt sections 1-2 and primary-source comparison.
detailed_claim_record.falsifier: A finite-N configuration count contradicting the binomial multiplicity or a failure of the stated Laplace-principle pressure limit under these parameters.

detailed_claim_record.claim: At beta=1,h=0, M_N/N^(3/4) converges to density proportional to exp(-x^4/12); Var(M_N)=(C2+o(1))N^(3/2), where C2=sqrt(12)Gamma(3/4)/Gamma(1/4)=1.1708286566..., and chi_N=Var(M_N)/N=(C2+o(1))sqrt(N).
detailed_claim_record.quantifiers: As N tends to infinity through all integers; chi_N is dimensionless response to h as it appears in the Gibbs exponent. Moment asymptotics use uniform quartic-tail control, not weak convergence alone.
detailed_claim_record.constants_costs: The limit law is one-dimensional and non-Gaussian; E[X^4]=3 and standardized kurtosis is 2.1884396152..., not 3. The exact finite-N baseline costs O(N) weight evaluations.
detailed_claim_record.evidence: Primary critical limit and O(N^-1/2) Kolmogorov rate in Eichelsbacher-Lowe 2010, Theorem 1.3; gamma moments evaluated directly. See RESULT.txt section 4.
detailed_claim_record.falsifier: An exact-binomial sequence whose scaled second moment fails to approach C2 or whose variance-normalized fourth moment fails to approach 2.1884396152... .

detailed_claim_record.claim: For every compact K subset R^2, beta_N=1+a/sqrt(N), h_N=b/N^(3/4), and (a,b) in K, the jittered law of M_N/N^(3/4) converges uniformly in total variation to density proportional to exp(-x^4/12+a*x^2/2+b*x).
detailed_claim_record.quantifiers: For each fixed compact K, sup_{(a,b) in K} d_TV(L(X_N+U_N),nu_(a,b)) tends to zero, where U_N is independent uniform on [-N^(-3/4),N^(-3/4)]. Every fixed polynomial moment converges uniformly. No rate is asserted.
detailed_claim_record.constants_costs: Uniform compact local expansion error O_{K,R}(N^-1/2) on |x|<=R; global tails are controlled by exp(-x^4/12+K_1*x^2/2+K_1*|x|). Exact-law computation is O(N) arithmetic operations. The statement with b varying uniformly is internally reconstructed here; the inspected primary finite-size theorem is b=0.
detailed_claim_record.evidence: Stirling expansion of the exact binomial mass plus the inequality I(m)>=m^2/2+m^4/12; RESULT.txt section 3.
detailed_claim_record.falsifier: One compact K and sequence (a_N,b_N) in K with jittered TV distance bounded below by a positive constant, or a contradiction to local expansion (7).

detailed_claim_record.claim: For each fixed beta>1 at h=0, M_N/N converges to the equal mixture at +/-m_beta, Var(M_N)/N^2 tends to m_beta^2, and chi_N is asymptotic to m_beta^2*N; conditioning on one stable phase recovers a local Gaussian fluctuation law.
detailed_claim_record.quantifiers: Fixed beta>1, h=0, N tending to infinity; m_beta is the positive solution m=tanh(beta*m). The conditional Gaussian is centered at +/-N*m_beta on sqrt(N) scale, with variance [I''(m_beta)-beta]^-1.
detailed_claim_record.constants_costs: Global susceptibility is order N due to between-phase variance; the local within-phase variance is finite. A field h_N=c/N yields weights exp(+-c*m_beta)/(2 cosh(c*m_beta)).
detailed_claim_record.evidence: Variational two-maximizer argument and two-well Laplace expansion; primary multiple-phase/conditioning source Ellis-Newman-Rosen 1980. See RESULT.txt section 5.
detailed_claim_record.falsifier: Failure of concentration at the two global maximizers, or a field-layer limit inconsistent with the two Laplace weights.

detailed_claim_record.claim: A single Gaussian CLT around the finite-volume mean does not hold uniformly through the CW critical point or the zero-field coexistence region; the correct limits are quartic at beta=1 and a two-phase mixture at fixed beta>1.
detailed_claim_record.quantifiers: Critical counterexample beta=1,h=0; coexistence counterexample any fixed beta>1,h=0. At criticality M_N/sqrt(N) is not tight and variance-standardized kurtosis tends 2.1884396152...; at coexistence M_N/N tends equal atoms at +/-m_beta.

detailed_claim_record.evidence: Exact binomial law and limits in RESULT.txt sections 3-5; primary sources Eichelsbacher-Lowe 2010 and Ellis-Newman-Rosen 1980.

scope: dilute Bose gas to Gross–Pitaevskii hierarchy audit
claim: The fixed-k GP hierarchy theorem is reconstructed; admissible product states rule out uniform convergence through k=N and any universal algebraic rate from qualitative assumptions alone.

interface.space: Symmetric N-boson wave functions in L2(R^(3N))
interface.potential: V >= 0, smooth, radial, compactly supported; source requires its dimensionless rho to be sufficiently small
interface.scattering: (-Delta + V/2)f0=0, f0 -> 1, a0=lim |x|(1-f0); scattering length of N^2 V(Nx) is a0/N
interface.initial_data_high_moments: For every m>=1, <psi_N,H_N^m psi_N> <= C^m N^m and fixed-k marginals condense to |phi><phi| tensor k
interface.initial_data_low_energy: <psi_N,H_N psi_N> <= C N and for every fixed k, ||psi_N - phi tensor k tensor xi_N^(N-k)|| -> 0
interface.observable: Fixed-k reduced density gamma_N,t^(k), tested against compact J^(k) on L2(R^(3k))
interface.time: Every fixed real t; convergence is locally uniform on compact time intervals for each fixed k

claims.claim: Under the stated repulsive GP scaling, energy and condensation assumptions, every fixed-k reduced density converges to the factorized solution of the cubic GP equation with coefficient 8*pi*a0.
claims.quantifiers: For each fixed k and each fixed t in R; the source proves compact-time convergence in the fixed-k weak* metric.

claims.claim: The exact scattering rescaling gives coefficient 8*pi*a0: N V_N(x) f_N(x) converges distributionally to 8*pi*a0 delta_0.
claims.quantifiers: Fixed smooth compactly supported radial V; f_N(x)=f0(Nx); N tends to infinity.
claims.proof: Change variables y=Nx and use integral V(y)f0(y)dy=8*pi*a0.

claims.claim: The cutoff H^k estimate supplies the hierarchy regularity needed for uniqueness.
claims.quantifiers: For each fixed integer k, rho sufficiently small, ell >> N^(-1/2), and N >= N0(k,C0).
claims.estimate: <psi,(H_N+N)^k psi> >= C0^k N^k integral Theta_(k-1)^(k)|nabla_1...nabla_k psi|^2 plus nonnegative derivative and potential terms.
claims.cutoff_window: Choose N ell^2 -> infinity, N ell^3 -> 0, and N ell^(3-epsilon) -> 0; ell=N^(-2/5), epsilon=1/4 is admissible.
claims.limit_consequence: Tr product_j(1-Delta_j) gamma_infinity,t^(k) <= C1^k with C1 independent of k and t on fixed compact intervals.
claims.source: Annals 2010, Proposition 5.3, Proposition 6.3, equations (5.29)-(5.33) and (6.12)-(6.13); uniqueness: arXiv:math-ph/0508010 v3, Theorem 9.1.

claims.claim: The proof's cutoff estimate is a fixed-k limit and does not provide a prelimit bound uniform for k growing with N.
claims.quantifiers: The estimate has N0=N0(k,C0), cutoff exponent 2^k*ell^(-epsilon), and Prop. 6.3 takes N to infinity for each fixed k.
claims.consequence: Do not interchange the fixed-k limit with a supremum over 1<=k<=N.

claims.claim: At the matched weaker-interaction scaling 0<beta<1/2 with the same V and product initial state, the effective coefficient is integral V rather than 8*pi*a0.
claims.quantifiers: For each fixed beta in (0,1/2), under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1 of the primary baseline source.
claims.source: Erdos-Schlein-Yau, arXiv:math-ph/0508010 v3, Theorem 1.1; Annals 2010, Section 2.

claims.claim: No universal algebraic fixed-k convergence rate follows from the qualitative initial condensation and O(N) energy assumptions of Theorem 2.2.
claims.quantifiers: There is no delta>0 and universal constant bounding all admissible one-body errors by O(N^(-delta)).
claims.counterexample: For orthonormal smooth compactly supported phi,chi, set phi_N=sqrt(1-epsilon_N^2)phi+epsilon_N chi and psi_N=phi_N tensor N, with epsilon_N=1/log(N+2). Then the energy is O(N), the fixed-k strong factorization holds, and the one-body trace-norm error at t=0 is exactly 2/log(N+2).

claims.claim: Uniform-in-k convergence over every 1<=k<=N is false even within the low-energy theorem's initial-data class.
claims.quantifiers: A single admissible sequence has sup_(1<=k<=N) trace-norm error bounded away from zero at t=0.
claims.counterexample: Use the same product family with epsilon_N=N^(-1/2). For k=N, the trace-norm distance from |phi tensor N><phi tensor N| is 2*sqrt(1-(1-1/N)^N), tending to 2*sqrt(1-e^(-1)).

falsifier.target_stronger_claims: A universal algebraic convergence rate from only qualitative condensation, or convergence uniformly over all k<=N.
falsifier.decisive_observation: Both failures occur at t=0 for the explicit smooth product sequences in C6 and C7, which satisfy the O(N) energy and fixed-k factorization assumptions.

claims.claim: There are smooth positive probability densities f_eps on R^3 with exactly the same mass, momentum, and kinetic energy as the unit Maxwellian M, such that H(f_eps|M)=O(eps^3)=o(eps^2), but integral |v|^2 v f_eps dv tends to e_1 rather than 0.
claims.construction: f_eps=(1-delta_eps)N(b_eps e_1,s_eps^2 I_3)+delta_eps N(R_eps e_1,I_3), with R_eps=eps^-3, delta_eps=eps^9, b_eps=-delta_eps R_eps/(1-delta_eps), c_eps=eps^3, and s_eps^2=1-c_eps/[3(1-delta_eps)]-c_eps^2/[3R_eps^2(1-delta_eps)^2].
claims.evidence: RESULT.txt Sections 2 and 5

detailed_claim_record.claim: For N=3, B=Phi(|v-v_*|)b(cos(theta)), -3<gamma<=1, two-sided Phi(r)~r^gamma bounds, and two-sided angular bounds b(cos(theta))~theta^(-2-alpha) with 0<alpha<2, the linearized Boltzmann Dirichlet form around a fixed Maxwellian controls (i) the weighted L2 norm of h-P h from Theorem 1.1 and (ii) the local H^(alpha/2) norm of h-P h from Theorem 1.2. In particular b(theta)=a theta^(-2-2s), gamma=0, alpha=2s, 0<s<1 gives local H^s_v control for Maxwell molecules.
detailed_claim_record.quantifiers_and_interface: For each admissible kernel B and every h in D(L_B), D_B(h)>=C_{gamma,alpha}||h-P h||^2_{H^(alpha/2)_loc(R^3)}. Precisely, for each fixed finite velocity ball B_R, this gives a positive c_R(B)>0 controlling the H^(alpha/2)(B_R) norm. P is the L2(M)-orthogonal projection onto span{1,v_1,v_2,v_3,|v|^2}. The theorem is velocity-only and has no spatial or time variable.
assumptions: N=3 and B=Phi(|v-v_*|)b(cos(theta))
-3<gamma<=1 and C_Phi r^gamma<=Phi(r)<=C'_Phi r^gamma for positive constants
0<alpha<2 and c_b theta^(-2-alpha)<=b(cos(theta))<=c'_b theta^(-2-alpha)
fixed homogeneous Maxwellian; source convention F=M(1+h), L2(M dv)
h belongs to the domain of the linearized operator
detailed_claim_record.proof_evidence: Primary source theorem read directly. Its proof restricts velocities to B_R, uses Carleman representation to lower-bound the positive jump term by the fractional difference integral with kernel |v-v'|^(-3-alpha), controls the cancellation remainder by a second-order Taylor expansion, and closes the L2 error with the Maxwell-molecule spectral gap. Near grazing angles the remainder is finite because integral_0^1 theta^(1-alpha)dtheta<infinity.

acquired: proof mechanism and equilibrium rescaling from the source paper

detailed_claim_record.constant_dependence: The primary source states constructive dependence on gamma, alpha, radial and angular kernel comparison constants, and N. For the exact angular multiplier a, D_a=a D_1, hence the best local coercivity constant scales exactly linearly with a. For a lower angular multiplier a_- and radial lower bound C_Phi, positivity gives a valid lower coefficient at least C_Phi*a_- times the reference-kernel coefficient. The cancellation remainder in the source proof contains an angular integral O((1-s)^(-1)) when alpha=2s, so that proof does not furnish a uniform endpoint bound as s approaches 1. No optimal asymptotic in s was extracted.
detailed_claim_record.costs: Infinite-dimensional functional input, no oracle or sample acquisition, and no finite bit or runtime cost. The constant is constructive at fixed parameters but no numerical lower bound was extracted here. The proof reports local ball constants with possible exponential growth in R.
detailed_claim_record.strongest_comparator: Gressman-Strain 2011 Lemma 2.5 gives a stronger global anisotropic geometric fractional coercivity estimate in N^(s,gamma), under a closely matching non-cutoff kernel class.
detailed_claim_record.falsifier: For one admissible fixed kernel and fixed finite R, construct h_j in D(L_B) with P h_j=0 and D_B(h_j)/||h_j||^2_{H^s(B_R)} tending to zero. Such a sequence would contradict the stated theorem.

detailed_claim_record.claim: For a fixed homogeneous Maxwellian and x-independent collision kernel on T_L^3, local velocity coercivity lifts mode by mode: for every fixed R, L^-3 integral_T D(h(x,.))dx >= c_R(s,a) sum_{m in Z^3} ||(I-P)h_hat_m||^2_{H^s(B_R)}. The constant is independent of L and the spatial mode m.
detailed_claim_record.quantifiers_and_interface: Fix 0<s<1, a>0, R<infinity, and L>0. Let h belong to L2(T_L^3;D(L_B)) and let h_hat_m be its normalized Fourier coefficients at k_m=2 pi m/L. Then the displayed inequality holds, initially for finite Fourier sums and by density for the stated domain. The spatial measure is normalized by L^-3; with unnormalized measure both sides acquire L^3.
assumptions: same kernel and Maxwellian as the primary local coercivity theorem
collision operator acts only in v and is independent of x
fixed homogeneous equilibrium parameters rho,u,T
Fourier coefficients and D are in the domain needed for Parseval
detailed_claim_record.proof: Since the collision form is local in x and quadratic, Parseval gives L^-3 integral D(h(x,.))dx=sum_m D(h_hat_m). Apply the primary source theorem to each coefficient; apply it separately to real and imaginary parts for complex modes. P acts only in v and is independent of m, so the sum of the mode inequalities is exactly the claim. No estimate of x derivatives is used.
detailed_claim_record.constant_dependence: For B=a theta^(-2-2s) and gamma=0, c_R scales as a. Under Maxwellian M_{rho,u,T}, let lambda=sqrt(2T) and z=(v-u)/lambda. The source scaling is D_{rho,u,T}(h)=rho^2/pi^3 * lambda^gamma D_base(h(u+lambda z)); in z coordinates the coefficient for gamma=0 is rho^2/pi^3, independent of T and u. For physical v-patch norms, the L2 and homogeneous H^s pieces carry rho^2 lambda^(-3) and rho^2 lambda^(2s-3), respectively, on the patch B_{lambda R}(u). A positive lower density bound is necessary. The modewise c_R has no torus-length dependence.
detailed_claim_record.costs: No new oracle, finite sample, or numerical computation. The derivation is one Parseval identity plus the source theorem; no arithmetic precision or conditioning cost is incurred. If the equilibrium parameters vary with x, Fourier modes couple and this corollary no longer follows as stated.
detailed_claim_record.strongest_comparator: Gressman-Strain 2011 Lemma 2.5 controls a global anisotropic velocity norm and is stronger than the local isotropic H^s mode estimate. The current claim is useful only as an exact fixed-equilibrium Fourier lift.
detailed_claim_record.falsifier: An admissible x-independent collision form for which Parseval fails to diagonalize the quadratic form, or a mode violating the source theorem, would refute the claim. For variable rho(x), u(x), or T(x), a counterexample to naive mode diagonalization is expected and that case is excluded.

detailed_claim_record.claim: No positive lower bound ||(L_B+i v.k)q||_L2(M)>=c||q||_L2(M) can hold uniformly over all nonzero Fourier modes on tori of arbitrary side length L, even for the selected Maxwell-molecule non-cutoff kernel.
detailed_claim_record.quantifiers_and_interface: For every L>0 choose k_L=(2 pi/L)e_1 and q(v)=1 in the relative-perturbation convention. With source Maxwellian M=e^(-|v|^2), ||(L_B+i v.k_L)q||/||q||=sqrt(2)pi/L, which tends to zero as L tends to infinity.
detailed_claim_record.proof: The constant function q=1 is a collision invariant, so L_B q=0. Thus (L_B+i v.k_L)q=i(2 pi/L)v_1. The Gaussian M has variance 1/2 in v_1, so ||v_1||_L2(M)/||1||_L2(M)=1/sqrt(2). The ratio is sqrt(2)pi/L. Therefore any proposed L-independent positive coercivity constant is contradicted by this explicit sequence.
assumptions: same homogeneous Maxwellian and kernel as above
streaming operator v dot grad_x
nonzero spatial Fourier mode k_L
detailed_claim_record.constant_dependence: The residual is exactly proportional to |k_L|=2 pi/L. The collision dissipation of the test vector is zero at every L. The inverse mean-zero torus Poincare scale is L^2/(4 pi^2).
detailed_claim_record.costs: Closed-form calculation only; no numerical experiment, oracle, or approximation.
detailed_claim_record.strongest_comparator: The modewise collision coercivity estimate controls only (I-P)q. Standard hypocoercivity estimates must add transport-macro coupling and retain the low-frequency torus scale; the local collision theorem contains no full-generator coercivity claim.
detailed_claim_record.falsifier: A verified identity L_B 1 != 0 under the stated linearization, or a different norm in which the displayed Gaussian ratio stays bounded below as L grows, would invalidate this counterexample. Neither applies to the stated interface.
